content: Neuron-only Wwox deletion in mouse (OPCs wild-type) gives reduced oligodendrocyte maturation, fewer myelinated axons, impaired axonal conductivity, decreased myelination-gene transcripts in cortex and hippocampus.
anchor: L9, L17, L121, Summary and Finding 1

content: Because OPCs retain WWOX yet fail to mature, the proximate lesion is a missing or distorted neuron-derived signal, not intrinsic WWOX loss in the oligodendrocyte lineage.
anchor: L9, L19, L110, Summary and Finding 1

content: Knowledge-base edge "Loss of WWOX Scaffold Function to Impaired Oligodendrocyte Maturation" is annotated INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES; the neuron-to-OPC signal is unidentified.
anchor: L9, L17, L37, L140, Summary, Findings 1 and 5
note: report reads the annotation as WWOX not acting directly inside maturing OLs

content: If the block were intrinsic to oligodendrocytes only WWOX restoration could help; a signalling failure upstream of intact OPCs allows pharmacological bypass.
Myelination can plausibly be rescued without restoring WWOX; lead candidate is a selective GSK-3beta inhibitor.
anchor: L13, L24, L166, Summary, Finding 2, Conclusion

content: WWOX normally restrains GSK-3beta; WWOX loss hyperactivates GSK-3beta in cortex, hippocampus and cerebellum.
note: labelled KB at L64 and L69

content: Lithium abolishes induced seizures in Wwox-/- mice.
anchor: L13, L22, L69, L146, Findings 2 and 8

content: GSK-3beta sits at centre of Wnt/beta-catenin control of OPC differentiation; review states GSK-3beta inhibition affects beta-catenin stability and is associated with OL differentiation.
Glycyrrhizic acid promoted oligodendrocyte maturation through modulating GSK-3beta signalling pathways.
Naringin regulates OPC differentiation and promotes remyelination through the beta-catenin/GSK-3beta pathway.
Convergence: the node hyperactivated by WWOX loss is an established promyelinating target; inhibiting it relieves a brake WWOX loss tightened, a WWOX-independent rescue.

In vivo, GSK3beta negatively regulates OL differentiation and myelination; inhibitors ARA-014418, lithium, indirubin, L803-mt increase OPs and OLs and promote myelination in postnatal mouse brain and optic nerve via beta-catenin nuclear translocation, CREB activation, Notch1 suppression.
note: called "strongest single piece of mechanistic support"

content: One WWOX-independent agent class (GSK-3beta inhibition, lithium) may address both seizure and myelin arms downstream of WWOX; "unusually favorable therapeutic position".
anchor: L13, L69, L146, L166, Summary, Finding 8, Conclusion

content: Selective GSK-3beta inhibitor (unnamed) as lead candidate; preferred over lithium for mechanistic attribution.
anchor: L13, L146, L161, Summary, Limitations, Follow-up

content: Lithium as GSK-3beta inhibitor: anti-seizure in Wwox-/- and promyelinating; supportive rationale, not primary probe.
ARA-014418, indirubin, L803-mt named as GSK-3beta inhibitors promoting myelination.
Natural-product GSK-3beta modulators (glycyrrhizic acid, naringin) listed as part of the inhibitor class.
Lithium is pleiotropic with a narrow therapeutic index in a paediatric/developmental population; selective inhibitors preferable.
note: safety statement in report; no source

content: No direct test of a GSK-3beta inhibitor on the WWOX myelin phenotype; GSK-3beta promyelination evidence is from non-WWOX systems; WWOX-GSK3b-myelin chain not closed in one study.
Framing A: loss of a positive activity-dependent cue (neuregulin/BDNF to NMDA-receptor signalling on oligodendrocyte lineage), degraded by WWOX-null E/I imbalance and impaired conduction.
anchor: L11, L27, L74-86, L115, Summary, Finding 3, Model

content: Neuregulin switches OLs from activity-independent to activity-dependent myelination by increasing NMDA receptor currents in OL-lineage cells 6-fold.
note: title row says "Neuregulin/BDNF"; BDNF not in quote

content: Remyelination after white-matter damage is NMDA-receptor-dependent.
WWOX-null cortex shows disrupted excitatory/inhibitory balance and impaired axonal conductivity.
E/I disruption or impaired conduction could degrade the activity-dependent signal reaching OPCs.
Clemastine, FDA-approved pro-myelinating agent via Akt-mTOR, OPC-intrinsic; WWOX-agnostic comparator that bypasses the neuronal supply.
anchor: L13, L29, L51, L107, Summary, Findings 3 and 5

content: Clemastine restored oligodendrogenesis, myelination, synaptic integrity, neuronal activity and cognitive performance in Pdk1 icKO mice.
note: rescue of genetic myelin defect without restoring gene

content: Clemastine independently preserves white matter and neurons after stroke via promyelination.
Thyroid hormone T3 as maturation-stage-specific, PPARalpha-linked, WWOX-agnostic comparator.
T3 promotes remyelination by enhancing OL maturation and attenuating astrogliosis; PDGFRa progenitor markers unaffected while myelin protein and mature OL numbers rose.
T3 acts on maturing oligodendrocytes via nuclear receptors controlling myelination genes.
T3 rescues anaesthetic-induced (S-ketamine) hypomyelination via PPARalpha pathway in OPCs; lesion mainly affects OPC-to-mature OL differentiation.
T3 is a precision tool to confirm the WWOX lesion sits at maturation rather than proliferation or sheath biogenesis.
note: presumes T3 rescue localises the block

content: WWOX lesion is a differentiation/maturation failure with reduced myelination-gene transcripts, so T3 is a natural comparator.
KB resolves the myelin arm into four nodes: impaired OL maturation (GO:0048709 down), CNS hypomyelination (GO:0042552 down), impaired axonal conductivity, neocortical network hypersynchrony.
AAV9-SynI-WWOX gene therapy rescues myelination.
Gene therapy restores WWOX so cannot separate missing signal from intrinsic block; positive control only (non-probative).
anchor: L13, L37, L109, L166, Finding 5, Model

content: Deletion-site x drug factorial: Arm A neuron-specific Wwox deletion (WT OPCs); Arm B oligodendrocyte-lineage deletion (Olig2/NG2/Sox10-Cre); each plus/minus drug; AAV9-WWOX positive control.

Four-level readout ladder: maturation (Sox10/CC1+ counts; MBP, PLP, MAG transcripts); sheath (g-ratio, MBP+ internode length on EM); conduction (CAP latency/velocity); network (video-EEG seizure frequency, slice bursting).
note: Audit: "MBP+ internode length on EM" is not an EM measure; MBP labelling is immunofluorescence, EM gives g-ratio and myelinated-axon counts

content: Decision rule: drug restores maturation to sheath in Arm A means missing neuronal signal is limiting and bypassable; Arm B reproducing the block and resisting the drug means intrinsic WWOX requirement.
Probe signal hypothesis by comparing neuregulin/activity-dependent (NMDA) manipulation against an OPC-intrinsic driver (T3 or clemastine).

Framing B: excess early neuronal activity in hyperexcitable WWOX-null cortex is itself anti-myelinating, suppressing OPC differentiation; links seizure and myelin arms ("most important conceptual advance").
anchor: L11, L58-61, L116, L166, Summary, Finding 6, Conclusion

content: Early in development decreased neuronal activity increases OL differentiation and enhanced activity reduces it, with AMPA-receptor signalling gating later maturation steps.
WWOX-null / neuronal-deletion cortex is hyperexcitable (raised EPSC amplitude, depolarised resting potential, higher AP frequency, network bursting) and hypomyelinated in the same animals.
note: PMID 34634460 described as WWOX-null cortex; whether neuron-specific not stated

content: Classic "activity promotes myelination" is stage- and neuregulin-dependent (adult/NMDA mode) and does not override the early-development inverse rule applying to the WWOX disease window.
note: adult attribution of the neuregulin mode is asserted by the report

content: PMID 24391468 (activity promotes myelination) superficially conflicts with the inverse rule; resolved by stage/mode dependence, so factorial must be read at defined developmental timepoint.
An intervention dampening early hyperexcitability (GSK-3beta inhibition/lithium being anti-seizure) could relieve the myelin block as a consequence.

Oligodendrocyte-intrinsic WWOX loss is called untested, the mouse model "formally silent" on it, and "Arm B of the proposed design has not been performed" (L142); human biallelic loss in all lineages means an intrinsic part cannot be excluded.
note: L142 sentence on Arm B added after audit; contradicted in part by the Olig2-Cre arm of the source paper (see reconcile E37, E47)

content: Intrinsic route 1: OPC-intrinsic GSK-3beta hyperactivation suppresses beta-catenin-dependent differentiation.

Intrinsic route 2: WWOX carries an SDR domain; myelin is lipid-rich; T3 maturation operates via lipid-sensing PPARalpha in OPCs, nominating a lipid-synthesis route for sheath impairment; also "loss of SDR/lipid scaffold function" in diagram.
note: SDR-domain statement has no citation; diagram labels it a branch of neuronal loss

content: Model: neuronal WWOX loss leads in parallel to de-repressed GSK-3beta, E/I imbalance and hyperexcitability, and loss of SDR/lipid scaffold function; all converge on impaired OPC maturation then hypomyelination, then conduction, then network hypersynchrony.
Because the OL lineage is intact in the decisive model, every downstream level is reachable without touching WWOX provided the intervention acts below the WWOX lesion.
The two framings predict opposite-sign manipulations: increase targeted activity-dependent signalling/clemastine bypass versus dampen hyperexcitability.
Neuron-to-OPC signal still molecularly unidentified; candidates nominated (neuregulin/NMDA; early hyperexcitability via AMPARs) but not established.
Stage specificity under-controlled; activity-myelination rule flips between developmental and adult states; cross-stage comparisons could invert conclusions.
Dismech KB holds 55+ disorders with shared Wnt/GSK-3beta and hypomyelination mechanisms; systematic comparison not completed.
Supporting Wnt/GSK-3beta remyelination literature: Foxg1 deletion accelerates remyelination via GSK-3beta/Wnt, abolished by SB216763.
Enriched-environment remyelination acts through PI3K/AKT/GSK3beta.
BSYS-exosome remyelination operates through miR-15b/Wnt/beta-catenin with changes in p-GSK3beta.

Close WWOX-GSK3b-myelin chain: in neuronal-deletion animals quantify OPC-lineage beta-catenin/Wnt target genes, test whether a selective GSK-3beta inhibitor restores maturation and sheath, confirming WWOX not restored.

Discriminate sign of neuronal signal: chemogenetic dampening of early cortical hyperexcitability versus neuregulin/NMDA-enhancing manipulation in neuron-specific Wwox-null cortex, scoring OPC differentiation at fixed early window.
Test lipid/SDR intrinsic route: in OL-lineage Wwox-null OPCs assay myelin-lipid synthesis and PPARalpha-pathway output plus/minus T3; test whether sheath metrics selectively impaired.
Prioritise selective GSK-3beta inhibitor over lithium for mechanistic trials; lithium's dual action as supportive rationale only.
Mine dismech KB for other disorders with convergent Wnt/GSK-3beta hypomyelination to test whether the bypass logic generalises or is WWOX-specific.
Treat each arm plus/minus selective GSK-3beta inhibitor, clemastine and T3 with AAV9-SynI-WWOX positive control (full factorial instruction).
